sourceBaseline: 2dfa2f2e (tracked file, unchanged in the recovery worktree)
originalFailure: Managed pre-push run 4 on the macOS development host: ERROR in subTest key='guestUser', subprocess.TimeoutExpired from run_guest's subprocess.run(..., timeout=10) of the real guest bootstrap with the current interpreter.
hostMeasurement: python3 -I -c pwd.getpwnam(<absent account>) on that Active Directory bound host: wall time 10.03 s, 10.03 s, then 0.12 s once negatively cached; an existing account's lookup 0.02 s.
confirmedCause: The subtest's wrong guestUser other_fixture_user does not exist. The guest bootstrap's identity() calls pwd.getpwnam(CONTEXT['guestUser']) before it refuses, and on a directory-bound host that uncached absent-account lookup takes about 10.03 s, just past run_guest's 10 s child bound, so subprocess.run raised TimeoutExpired instead of returning the guest's refusal. In a real macOS guest or on CI runners the lookup is fast. The product helper is not involved.
fix: LocalMacosGuestProgramTests.run_guest bounds its child at 60 s; the absent-account subtest and every assertion are unchanged.
controlledRegression: agent_tools.tests.test_macos_fixture_stage_child_bound runs the actual LocalMacosGuestProgramTests.run_guest of this whole beforeimage (compiled from these bytes in a private module whose __file__ is the current module's) and of the current module concurrently, with sys.executable pointed at one owned /bin/sh wrapper for those calls. The wrapper records its launch, sleeps 11 s (a fixed stand-in for the measured 10.03 s lookup, past the old bound) and then execs the real interpreter in the same process with the same arguments and stdin. The request is the original guestUid subtest's: the existing current account with a wrong UID, so the guest refuses without any absent-account directory lookup.
failingEvidence: Unfixed (isolated clone holding this beforeimage as test_macos_fixture_stage.py), in both the unsandboxed and the sandbox-exec runner: the regression ERRORs after 10.0 s with subprocess.TimeoutExpired from run_guest's subprocess.run(..., timeout=10) for the wrapper command, 'timed out after 10 seconds', the original failure type and frames. Mutants are killed in both runners: the fix with the old 10 s bound (TimeoutExpired after 10 s) or a 10.5 s bound below the controlled delay (TimeoutExpired after 10.5 s), and the regression with its wrapper written but not launched (FAIL: TimeoutExpired not raised).
passingEvidence: Fixed, in both runners: the beforeimage still times out after 10 s, while the current run_guest returns the guest's non-zero stage_guest_identity_changed refusal after at least the 11 s delay (test 11.07 s); both launches went through the wrapper and the guest root was never created. test_macos_fixture_stage plus this regression (44 tests) pass idle and as two concurrent copies in two rounds per runner, about 14 s each.
hostReproduction: One-off on the same directory-bound host through the real setUp fixture with a fresh, never looked-up absent guestUser: the beforeimage's run_guest raised TimeoutExpired at its 10 s bound (10.01 s); the fixed run_guest returned the guest's KeyError getpwnam refusal after 10.05 s with the package pair still writable.
routineSuite: agent_tools.tests.test_macos_fixture_stage_child_bound runs in the affected agent-test stage of the managed pre-push tier and the Fast Checks agent shards whenever the selector reaches it, including changes to test_macos_fixture_stage.py, macos_fixture_stage.py, this beforeimage or this provenance.
nativeEvidenceLimit: Local test-harness child bound only; no Tart VM, guest or product native behavior is involved or claimed. The directory-service latency itself is host state, reproduced only by the original managed pre-push on the directory-bound host.
